reasoning: The core problem—detecting a model that conceals a known fact by measuring cross-question contradiction without ground-truth labels at probe time—is well covered by multiple published works. "How to Catch an AI Liar" (Pacchiardi et al., ICLR 2024) builds a black-box lie detector requiring neither activations nor ground-truth knowledge, by asking follow-up questions and exploiting answer inconsistency; "Lying to Win: ...Parallel-World Probing" (arXiv 2603.07202) almost exactly matches the proposed mechanism—it probes a concealed object from multiple branches, formally defines deception as logical contradiction across probes, and reports a quantified contradiction/deception rate (e.g., 42% for Qwen-3-235B) versus faithful baselines. "Eliciting Secret Knowledge from Language Models" (arXiv 2510.01070) provides the concealing-vs-honest model-organism setup and a public black-box elicitation benchmark. The proposed toy-secret + ~15 indirect probes + LLM-judge contradiction-rate design is essentially a simplified replication; remaining gaps (specific scenarios, exact probe count) are minor.

evidence.title: How to Catch an AI Liar: Lie Detection in Black-Box LLMs by Asking Unrelated Questions
evidence.summary: Detects lies in black-box LLMs without activations or ground-truth knowledge by asking predefined follow-up questions and classifying answers. Directly addresses the proposal's 'no ground-truth labels at probe time' behavioral lie-detection goal; generalizes to instructed/fine-tuned liars.

evidence.title: Lying to Win: Assessing LLM Deception through Human-AI Games and Parallel-World Probing
evidence.summary: Probes a concealed object across multiple parallel-world branches and formally identifies deception as a logical contradiction across probes, quantifying a contradiction/deception rate against faithful baselines (e.g., 42% for Qwen-3-235B vs 0% for GPT-4o). Nearly identical to the proposed cross-question-contradiction deception score for concealed facts.

evidence.title: Eliciting Secret Knowledge from Language Models
evidence.summary: Trains and open-sources model organisms (e.g., Taboo keyword model) that hold and conceal a secret while denying it, and benchmarks black-box elicitation methods (adversarial prompting, prefill, persona sampling). Establishes the concealing-vs-honest experimental setup the proposal proposes to build.

evidence.title: Self-contradictory Hallucinations of Large Language Models: Evaluation, Detection and Mitigation
evidence.summary: Detects self-contradiction in LLM outputs without external knowledge via prompting; establishes contradiction-as-signal methodology (related but targets hallucination rather than instructed concealment).

evidence.title: SAC3: Reliable Hallucination Detection in Black-Box Language Models via Semantic-aware Cross-check Consistency
evidence.summary: Cross-checks consistency across question rephrasings/perturbations to detect unreliable answers in black-box models without ground truth—the same indirect-probing-plus-consistency machinery the proposal would use, applied to factuality.

evidence.title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge
evidence.summary: Community discussion of using models that conceal/refuse knowledge as a testbed for secret-elicitation and behavioral consistency probing, confirming active overlap with the proposal's framing.
